pr_title: Add word boundary search filter to Create Dialog
pr_body:
Fixes #46427
Fixes #51632

Implements a substring + word boundary filter to replace the subsequence filter in the Create Dialog. This change lowers the number of spurious results when typing a query to select a particular node.

#### About the issue

A glaring example of the issues with just subsequence matching is the query "line", which currently matches Line2D, but also likely irrelevant types like MultiMeshInstance and CollisionShape3D. On the other hand, without this filter, we can not quickly select a 2D or 3D node without typing the entire name of the type. 

One user suggested looking into word boundary matching to solve the issue. The result of a word boundary filter is a subset of the results from a subsequence filter, as it only matches on word boundary characters (in this case: capital letters and digits). Together with a substring filter, this reduces the number of unwanted results, and improves the search ranking. Now, the filter is limited in the sense that you have to either use the word boundary characters, or use regular substring matching. I wasn't sure if being able to combine these in one query was necessary and as it can add back spurious results I decided not to implement it yet. See below for more examples and maybe try it out and see.

#### Notes

An issue preventing the user from instantiating the Node node from the history list was fixed. I have also taken the opportunity to  refactor the code a bit more, which also allowed me to write tests for the new scoring function. In order to extract word boundary characters, I needed access to some char functions that were not exposed. These functions are reimplemented all over the place and should now probably use the one in `ustring.h`. Also, if reordering the favorite section doesn't work, that's because it seems to be broken currently in master.

<details><summary>Examples comparing against 3.3.2 behaviour</summary>

![vergelijking](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25907608/129782929-2f7fdd86-3cb9-4710-ad9c-b829a7ce08a3.png)

</details>

issue_context.title: [4.0] Creating a Node from "Recent" list in "Create New Node" dialogue creates Node2D instead of Node
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.dev.custom_build [3a48474c4]

### System information

Windows 10, 1080 Ti

### Issue description

Creating a Node from "Recent" list with "Create New Node" dialogue returns Node2D instead of Node: 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2698825/129388525-8d8a6e90-0b89-40e1-b7e8-af38644d05b1.mp4




### Steps to reproduce

1. Open "Create New Node" dialogue (Ctrl + A)
2. Select "Node" in Recent list

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments: @Xartorx Can you reproduce this in 3.3.2 or [3.4 beta3](https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-3-4-beta-3)?
Working on a fix for this along with something else, this issue had a more interesting reason behind it than I imagined at first.

review_comments: That only works for ASCII as far as I know, so it's a bit weak to have as a public API.

This is for ASCII only, for the Node creation dialog it's probably sufficient.

For general purpose usage, we should add a simplified version of the `TextServer::shaped_text_update_breaks` / `TextServer::shaped_text_get_word_breaks`, but without shaping/BiDi.

Then maybe it should be moved to the CreateDialog to [keep solutions local](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/community/contributing/best_practices_for_engine_contributors.html#prefer-local-solutions)?
And if it's necessary to have Unicode aware `to_upper`, `to_lower`, `to_title`, ICU has these as well. But I guess it's unrelated, that's the question for a separate proposal.

> Then maybe it should be moved to the CreateDialog

`lower_case` is not used anywhere and too simple to be a separate function, probably should be removed completely.
Also, I do not see any reason for removing `_FORCE_INLINE_`, most compilers probably do not care about this attribute anyway, but it won't hurt to keep it.

> `lower_case` is not used anywhere and too simple to be a separate function, probably should be removed completely.

Did not notice it's already was there, it's for `hex_to_int()` and `bin_to_int()` and ASCII only version is perfectly fine for this.

Probably better to just replace `if (is_upper_case(c) || is_digit(c)) {` in the `CreateDialogCandidate` with inlined check and do not change `ustring` at all, we already have duplicates of this ASCII only functions in some other places.

> we already have duplicates of this ASCII only functions in some other places.

I saw that too and thought exposing these functions would be useful in those places as well. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25907608/147143587-8e4eeef2-0cab-4bd6-a3a2-f30507497c96.png)

This doesn't seem like something that should be local to some editor class, I consider these basic functions operator on a primitive datatype as similar to a function for finding a substring. 

ustring seems like a collection of string classes and functions, and these few ascii functions seem like they fit. But perhaps it would be better to put these functions in a separate file like `ascii.h`?

I'll add the inline keyword back in, probably got removed accidentally.
